name: Kekkon Shugi Kokka
source: In a fictional country that was once threatened by low birth rates and an aging population, a law was passed to enforce marriage at the age of 18. Failure to comply results in the death penalty — if you don’t get married by the day of high school graduation where marriage ceremonies are held nationwide, you are taken to the Bachelor Jail and executed. Kekkon Shugi Kokka is a collection of 8 short stories surrounding 16 teenagers who live under this law, in a country where “love” and “romance” are glorified to the point of brainwashing and marriage is a matter of life and death.
translation: 在一个虚构的国家里，低生育率与人口老龄化曾带来严重危机。为此，国家颁布法律，规定每个人必须在18岁时结婚，违者处以死刑。高中毕业当天，全国各地都会举行婚礼；如果到那一天你还没有结婚，就会被送进单身者监狱处决。《结婚主义国家》收录了八篇短篇故事，围绕生活在这项法律之下的16名少年少女展开。在这个国家，“爱”与“恋爱”被美化到了近乎洗脑的地步，而结婚则关乎生死。
